skill.name: Metaphor: what is meant
skill.why: Metaphors pack a big picture into a few words. You have to unpack them.
skill.how: Spot what can't be really true. Ask what the two things share.

steps.say: Gus looked into my room and said this. Rude!
show: Zed's bedroom is a rubbish tip.

options.text: Zed's room is very messy.
Zed's room has a real garbage truck in it.
options.reason: A garbage truck can't fit in a bedroom! Gus doesn't mean it's really true.

options.text: Zed's room is next door to the tip.
options.reason: Gus says the room IS a tip, not next to one. What's a tip full of?

steps.win: Yes! It isn't really a tip. Reading it as really true is called taking it literally.

steps.say: So how did I work it out? I asked: what do my room and a tip share?
steps.ask: What do the room and a tip share?

options.text: Both are full of junk.
Both smell like roses.
options.reason: Tips don't smell like roses! What is piled up in a tip?

options.text: Both have a big front gate.
options.reason: My room has a door, not a gate. What is piled up everywhere?

steps.win: Yes! Junk everywhere. Saying one thing IS another, with no like or as, is a metaphor.

steps.say: A simile says like. A metaphor just says it IS. Can you spot the difference?

show.text: My room is like a tip.
show.nudge: That one uses like, so it's a simile. Find the one with no like or as.
That one is plain. It's really true, with no picture in it.

steps.win: Yes! No like or as. It just says my room IS a tip.

steps.say: Careful! Gus thinks every metaphor needs the word is. But some hide in a doing word.

show.nudge: Mrs Patel is a real person. Look at what she did.

show.text: from the oven to the till.
show.nudge: The oven and the till are real. Which word can't be really true?

steps.ask: Tap the word that can't be really true.
steps.win: Yes! She isn't a bee. Buzzed is a metaphor. It shows she rushed about, very busy.

steps.say: Now you unpack one. Ask what the two things share.
steps.ask: What does bulldozed tell you about the captain?

options.text: He drove a real bulldozer onto the ground.
options.reason: That's taking it literally. No bulldozers allowed on the footy ground!

options.text: He pushed through hard, and nobody stopped him.
He walked slowly around the pack.
options.reason: A bulldozer goes straight through things, not around them.

steps.win: Yes! A bulldozer pushes through anything in its way. So did the captain.

steps.say: Last trick. The word is doesn't always mean a metaphor. Some sentences with is are really true.

show.nudge: That's really true. Sam really plays in goal.
That could be really true too. Find the one that can't be.

steps.ask: Tap the metaphor. Which one can't be really true?
steps.win: Yes! Sam can't be a real wall. It means nothing gets past her.

terms.means: Says a thing IS something else, or does what that thing does. No like or as.
What the writer is really talking about.
The different thing. Ask what the two things share.

examples: from the oven to the till.
card.test: Can it be really true? If not, ask what the two things share. That's what it means.

weDo.text: After the cross-country race, Tully's legs were two wet noodles. She flopped onto the grass and couldn't get up.
weDo.prompt: What does 'Tully's legs were two wet noodles' mean?
weDo.hint: Her legs can't really be noodles. What are wet noodles like?
weDo.success: Weak and floppy. Wet noodles flop about, and Tully can't even stand up.

options.text: Her legs felt weak and floppy.
Her legs were covered in noodles.
options.reason: That's taking it literally. Nobody spilled noodles on her.

options.text: Her legs were long and thin.
options.reason: Noodles can be long, but Tully flopped and couldn't get up. What are wet noodles like?

weDo.prompt: Put each sentence with the device it uses.
weDo.hint: Look for like or as first. No like or as? Check which part can't be really true.
weDo.success: Similes say one thing is like another. Metaphors say one thing is another.

items.text: The moon was a silver coin.
items.reason: It says the moon IS a coin, with no like or as.

items.text: Mo's laugh sounds like a kookaburra.
items.reason: It uses like to compare Mo's laugh with a bird, so it's a simile.

items.text: Zed's backpack is a black hole.
items.reason: It says the backpack IS a black hole, with no like or as. Things vanish in it.

items.text: The icy pole was as hard as a brick.
items.reason: It uses as ... as to compare the icy pole with a brick, so it's a simile.

items.text: Gus's room is a swamp.
items.reason: It says his room IS a swamp, with no like or as.

creature.name: Metapince
creature.blurb: A mangrove crab that never says something is like anything. It says it IS something, then waits for you to work out what it means.

write.ask: Combine these into one sentence with a metaphor. Say the bus IS something else, with no like or as.
given: The school bus was very crowded.
checks: I said the bus IS something else.
I used no like or as.
My picture shows how squashed everyone was.
write.model: The school bus was a sock drawer that wouldn't shut, with all of us squashed inside.

encounters.frame: Mo cooked dinner. The Metapince is hiding under the table.
encounters.text: Mo's soup was a swamp. It was green and brown, with lumps floating in it. Something bubbled up from the bottom. Gus poked it with a spoon. 'I think it moved,' he said. Tully held her nose. Mo said it was his nan's recipe. 'Did your nan like it?' asked Zed. 'Nobody knows,' said Mo. 'She never tried it.' Everyone had toast for dinner instead.
encounters.prompt: What does 'Mo's soup was a swamp' mean?
encounters.success: It looked murky and gross. Green, brown and lumpy, just like a swamp.

options.text: Mo cooked the soup in a swamp.
options.reason: The soup isn't really a swamp, and Mo didn't cook in one. What is a swamp like?

options.text: The soup looked murky and gross.
The soup was hot and spicy.
options.reason: The story never says how it tasted. Picture a swamp. What would the soup look like?

encounters.frame: Indi found a poem in the Soggy Biscuit's logbook. The Metapince is looking up.
encounters.text: Camping Out. The sky was a black blanket. It covered the whole bush. It was full of tiny holes. Light shone through each one. Dad pointed at the brightest hole. 'That's Sirius,' he said. 'It's the brightest star of all.' The fire popped. The frogs croaked. I counted the holes until I fell asleep. Dad fell asleep first. I got to forty-two.

encounters.success: Stars. The sky is a blanket, and the stars are holes with light shining through.

encounters.frame: Zed is writing about his gaming night. The Metapince wants to sort it.
encounters.prompt: Put each sentence with the device it uses.
encounters.success: Similes say one thing is like another. Metaphors say it IS the other thing. Plain facts do neither.

items.text: Zed's controller was a magic wand.
items.reason: It says the controller IS a wand, with no like or as.

items.text: Zed's bedroom was a dark cave.
items.reason: It says the bedroom IS a cave, with no like or as.

items.text: Mo was a statue on the couch.
items.reason: It says Mo IS a statue, with no like or as.

items.text: The screen glowed like a campfire.
items.reason: It compares using like, so it's a simile.

items.text: Zed's thumbs were as quick as mice.
items.reason: It compares using as, so it's a simile.

items.text: Zed likes games with loud music.
items.reason: Here 'likes' means enjoys. Nothing is being compared.

items.text: Mo was the winner of the first game.
items.reason: This is really true. Mo won, so it's a plain fact.

encounters.frame: A page from Leo's diary blew onto the Soggy Biscuit. The Metapince has its claws over its ears.
encounters.text: Dear Diary, My sister Bea got a violin for her birthday. It is brand new and shiny. She practises every afternoon in the lounge room. Her violin is a squeaky gate. Every note makes the dog howl. Dad has started wearing earmuffs. Mum says Bea will get better. I hope Mum is right. I also hope it's soon. Bea says I am just jealous. I'm not.
encounters.prompt: What does 'Her violin is a squeaky gate' mean?
encounters.success: It sounds awful. A squeaky gate screeches, and the dog howls at every note.

options.text: It is old and falling apart.
options.reason: The diary says it's brand new and shiny. What is a squeaky gate known for?

options.text: It makes a horrible, screechy sound.
It gets stuck and won't open.
options.reason: A violin doesn't open. What do you hear when a squeaky gate moves?

encounters.frame: Wren wrote about her first snorkel at the outer reef. The Metapince is reading it upside down.
encounters.text: The water was so clear that I could see all the way to the sandy bottom. Then I put my face in, and I forgot to breathe. The reef was a busy city. Hundreds of fish zipped past in every direction. A parrotfish crunched on coral, while tiny cleaner fish darted in and out of its mouth. Crabs scuttled along the cracks. An octopus slid out of one hole and squeezed into another. Not one of them stopped to look at me. They all had somewhere to be. Underwater, it was completely silent, except for the sound of my own breathing. I stayed out there until my fingers went wrinkly.
encounters.prompt: What does 'The reef was a busy city' mean?
encounters.success: It was crowded and busy. Hundreds of creatures rushed about, all with somewhere to be, like people in a city.

options.text: The water around the reef was dirty and polluted.
options.reason: Wren says the water was so clear she could see the bottom. What fills a busy city?

options.text: The reef was noisy, with lots of loud traffic.
options.reason: Wren says it was completely silent underwater. What else fills a busy city besides noise?

options.text: The reef was crowded with creatures rushing about.

encounters.frame: The Metapince is watching an egret fish in the shallows. Wren is taking notes.
encounters.text: FIELD NOTES, Mirage Mangroves, 7 am. A great egret landed in the shallow water at the edge of the channel this morning. It is the tallest bird I have seen on the island, and it is completely white. Its legs were two chopsticks, poking straight down into the water. It didn't move for nearly five minutes. Then its neck shot forward, and it came up with a small silver fish. It swallowed the fish whole, head first. A second later, it was standing perfectly still again, waiting for the next one. When a dinghy came past, it spread its wings and flew off across the mangroves.
encounters.prompt: What does 'Its legs were two chopsticks' tell you?
encounters.success: Its legs were long, thin and straight. That's what chopsticks are like, poking straight down.

options.text: Its legs were long, thin and straight.
Its legs were made of thin pieces of wood.
options.reason: That's taking it literally. Picture a chopstick. What shape is it?

options.text: It used its legs to pick up the fish.
options.reason: The egret caught the fish with its neck shooting forward, not its legs.

encounters.frame: Zed found this story in a bottle. The Metapince doesn't like the sound of it.
encounters.text: It was a warm, still night when Ollie rowed out to find the old shipwreck. His torch was in his pocket, and his heart was thumping. Halfway across the bay, the fog rolled in. Within a minute, the fog was a grey wall. Ollie couldn't see the shore. He couldn't see the wreck. He could barely see the end of his own oars. Somewhere close by, he heard a slow splash, then another. He held his breath and switched on his torch. The beam bounced straight back at him. Then something bumped the side of the boat. It was a pelican, looking very annoyed.
encounters.prompt: What does 'the fog was a grey wall' mean?
encounters.success: You couldn't see through it. Ollie can't even see the end of his oars.

options.text: The fog was freezing cold and damp.
options.reason: The story says it was a warm night. What happens when you stand in front of a wall?

options.text: The fog was too thick to see through.
The fog was hard enough to bump into.
options.reason: That's taking it literally. Something bumps the boat, but it's a pelican, not the fog.

encounters.frame: Zed is writing up the worst gaming night of his life. The Metapince is helping him tidy up.
encounters.text: Mum asked me to mind my little brother, Theo, for ten minutes while she hung out the washing. Theo is two, and he only comes up to my knees. I was halfway through the final level of Swamp Quest, so I sat him on the rug with a box of blocks and told him to be good. That was my first mistake. Theo was a hurricane in the lounge room. In five minutes he had tipped out the toy box, pulled every cushion off the couch, emptied a packet of crackers onto the carpet and unplugged the console, right before the boss fight. He did all of it without making a sound. When I finally turned around, he was sitting in the middle of the mess, giggling and wearing a cracker box as a hat. Mum walked in, looked at the room, then looked at me. I have lost my console for a week.
encounters.prompt: What does Zed mean when he says Theo was a hurricane in the lounge room?
encounters.success: A hurricane wrecks everything fast. In five minutes, Theo made a huge mess of the whole room.

options.text: Theo was angry with Zed and wanted to get back at him.
options.reason: Theo is giggling the whole time. The hurricane is about how fast he wrecked the room.

options.text: Theo was loud, screaming and crashing about the room.
options.reason: Zed says Theo did it all without making a sound. The hurricane is about the mess.

options.text: Theo made a huge mess of the whole room very quickly.
Theo was big and strong enough to knock things over.
options.reason: Theo is two and only comes up to Zed's knees. The hurricane is about the mess he made.

encounters.frame: Tully wrote a note about an astronaut's spacewalk diary. One word is wrong.
encounters.text: Spacewalk diary, Day 12. Today I went outside the space station for the first time, to fix a broken solar panel. Getting into the suit took nearly an hour. It is heavy, about 120 kilograms on Earth, although up here it floats. It is also surprisingly roomy, so I could wriggle my arms right out of the sleeves. Once I was outside, the sun beat down on me with nothing to block it. Inside, my suit was an oven. Sweat ran into my eyes, and I couldn't wipe it away because my helmet was in the way. It took me three hours to fix the panel. When I finally came back inside, my crewmates cheered, and I drank two whole bags of cold water in a row. Then I fell asleep, floating in my sleeping bag, before I had even finished my dinner. Tomorrow I'm going back out to fix the second panel.

encounters.frame: Poet Pip is reviewing the Mudflat Band. The Metapince is tapping along.
encounters.text: The Mudflat Band played on the boardwalk last night, and I have been humming ever since. There are four of them: a singer, two guitarists and a drummer called Barney. Barney is not the most popular member of the band. The others complain that he eats all the snacks before every show and never helps carry the speakers. But Barney is the heartbeat of the band. He sits at the back, playing softly and perfectly calm, and he never misses a beat. When the singer forgot her words in the third song, the guitarists watched Barney's sticks and stayed in time until she remembered. When the power cut out for a moment, Barney kept on drumming, and the whole band picked up again the second the lights came back. The crowd hardly noticed. Afterwards, the singer thanked everybody except Barney, who was already eating the leftover sausage rolls. I'll be at their next show, and I'm bringing my own snacks.
encounters.prompt: What does the reviewer mean by 'Barney is the heartbeat of the band'?
encounters.success: A heartbeat is steady and keeps everything going. Barney's steady beat keeps the whole band together.

options.text: He is the band member that everyone loves most.
options.reason: The others complain about him and the singer doesn't thank him. It's about his steady beat.

options.text: He plays so loudly that the crowd feels it in their chests.
options.reason: The review says he plays softly. The heartbeat is about keeping a steady beat.

options.text: He keeps a steady beat that the whole band follows.
He gets so nervous that his heart pounds on stage.
options.reason: The review says Barney is perfectly calm. The metaphor is about his drumming.

encounters.frame: Mo got a job helping in the school canteen. The Metapince is hiding in the bain-marie.
encounters.text: On my first day helping in the Crab Creek Primary canteen, Mrs Patel handed me an apron and said, 'Good luck.' I thought she was joking. Then the lunch bell rang. The canteen was a beehive. Three hundred kids squeezed through the door at once, all talking, all waving coins, all trying to get to the front. Mrs Patel buzzed from the oven to the till to the fridge without stopping. Two Year 6 helpers took orders, wrapped sausage rolls and poured drinks so fast I could hardly see their hands. The whole room smelled of hot chips and tomato sauce. Even so, not one person lost their temper. Nobody pushed, and a Prep kid even said thank you three times. But by the end of lunch, I had sold two hundred meat pies and dropped one on my foot. Mrs Patel says I can come back next week. I think I need a lie down.
encounters.prompt: In his first draft, Mo wrote 'The canteen was a zoo.' Why is 'a beehive' the better metaphor for this canteen?
encounters.success: A zoo sounds wild. A beehive is packed and busy, but the bees work calmly, like the friendly crowd.

options.text: A beehive is even louder than a zoo at feeding time.
options.reason: Both are noisy places. What does Mo say about how the kids behaved?

options.text: Bees make sweet honey, and the canteen sold treats.
options.reason: Mo says the room smelled of hot chips and sauce. Think about the crowd instead.

options.text: Bees are busy but work together, and everyone was friendly.
Bees sting, and the kids were cranky and pushy.
options.reason: Mo says nobody pushed, and a Prep kid said thank you three times.

encounters.frame: This sign stands at the start of the Mirage Mangroves boardwalk. The Metapince lives under it.
encounters.text: WELCOME TO THE MIRAGE MANGROVES BOARDWALK. Please stay on the boardwalk and keep dogs on a lead. Look down between the planks and you will see a tangle of roots poking out of the mud, some thin and some thick. It may look like a muddy, smelly swamp, but this forest is the nursery of the sea. When the tide comes in, thousands of baby fish, prawns and crabs swim in among the roots. The roots are too tight and twisted for big hungry fish to follow, so the babies can feed and grow in safety. Some will spend months here. When they are big enough, they swim out through the channel to the open water and the reef beyond, and many of the fish caught off the end of the jetty started their lives right under your feet. Nobody plants these trees or sells them; they have grown here on their own for hundreds of years. Scientists have counted more than fifty kinds of fish living in this one small forest. Please do not pull up seedlings, dig for crabs or throw rubbish into the water. Without these trees, there would be far fewer fish in the sea, so please help us protect them. Thank you for visiting.
encounters.prompt: Why does the sign call the forest 'the nursery of the sea' instead of just 'a forest'?
encounters.success: A nursery keeps babies safe. Picturing baby fish safe in the roots makes visitors want to protect the trees.

options.text: It tells visitors that young trees are grown here, so they can buy one.
options.reason: That's a plant nursery. The sign says nobody plants or sells these trees.

parts: Welcome back to the grand final, where the Reef Rays and the Crab Creek Pinchers are level with two minutes to go. It has rained all afternoon, and the mud is up to the players' ankles. The Rays are the youngest team in the league, and plenty of people said they would fall apart today. They haven't, and the reason is their captain, Priya. She is a lighthouse for this young team, guiding them through every storm.

parts.tap: Priya is the tallest player on the ground, a head above everyone else.
parts.reason: Lighthouses are tall, but Tully's metaphor is about guiding. Being tall doesn't steer anyone.

parts.tap: Her bright yellow boots glow through the mud and the rain.
parts.reason: A lighthouse shines, but glowing boots don't help anyone through a storm. What does Tully say Priya does?

parts.tap: She has called out every move today, and her teammates have followed each one.
She has stood in the same spot at centre half-back all game.
parts.reason: A lighthouse stands still, but staying in one spot doesn't guide a team. What do her teammates do?

parts: Now Jess has the ball, fifty metres out, and Priya points to the left. Jess runs left, steadies and kicks. It's high, it's long, it's straight through the middle! The siren goes, and the Reef Rays have won by a single point. My co-commentator, Bruce, has fallen off his chair. Folks, that was the greatest finish I have ever seen. Somebody get Bruce a glass of water.

encounters.frame: Gus wrote a note about Ruby's ghost story. One word is wrong.
encounters.text: Ruby had promised her cousins that she would walk through the old Mangrove Point cemetery at midnight, and she was not the kind of girl who broke a promise, even a stupid one. The night was dry and warm, and a light breeze carried the smell of salt up from the water. At the cemetery gate, she switched off her torch, because that was the rule. The path through the cemetery was a tunnel. The branches of the huge fig trees on either side met high above her head, so thick that not one scrap of moonlight got through. She could still feel the breeze on her arms, and she could hear everything: the owls calling, the crabs clicking in the mud, her own heart thudding in her ears. She walked with one hand out in front of her, counting her steps. At step one hundred and twelve, something cold and wet touched her fingers. Ruby screamed so loudly that every owl in the trees took off at once. Then she heard a familiar voice. 'Sorry,' said her cousin Archie, holding out a melting icy pole. 'I brought you a snack.' It was lime. Ruby ate it anyway, and her cousins have never let her forget it.

encounters.frame: Maxx Vantablack is live from Green Screen Swamp. Zed is recording it for evidence.
encounters.text: Vantafam! Maxx here, live from deep in the Mirage Mangroves, on my most dangerous rescue mission EVER. And I'm going to be honest with you, guys, because honesty is my brand: this swamp is a sauna. It's forty degrees, the air is thick and wet, and steam is literally rising off the mud. My makeup artist has redone my face four times, and I've sweated through three gold tracksuits since breakfast. Even my hairspray has given up. I haven't had one second to sit down and relax, because I've been rescuing Creatures nonstop, and before you ask, no, there's nowhere to wash out here either. I'm covered in mud from my sneakers to my eyebrows. My assistant has been fanning me with a palm leaf, but it's just pushing the hot air around. Honestly, I don't know how the Creatures survive in this. Which is why I'm rescuing them, obviously, and taking them somewhere with air-conditioning, like my yacht. Tomorrow I'm doing a special stream on my new cooling fan, the Maxx-Breeze, only ninety-nine dollars in the Vantamart. Anyway, smash that heart button so I know you care, and remember, two Xs, because one X is for losers. Stay gold!
encounters.prompt: Maxx ends by selling his Maxx-Breeze fan. Why does he call the swamp a sauna first?
encounters.success: A sauna is hot and steamy. Once fans picture that heat, Maxx's fan sounds like just what they need.

options.text: So the swamp sounds like a good spot to sit back and relax.
options.reason: Maxx says he hasn't sat down once. He wants the swamp to sound awful.

options.text: So fans know he can wash the mud off before the stream ends.
options.reason: Maxx says there's nowhere to wash, and he's muddy to his eyebrows.

options.text: So fans think the swamp has wooden benches and a heater.
options.reason: That's taking it literally. Maxx is describing the heat and steam, not furniture.

options.text: So the heat sounds unbearable, and a cooling fan sounds worth buying.

encounters.frame: Zed wrote this for the school newsletter. The Metapince is pressing all the buttons.
encounters.text: In the corner of the fish and chip shop on the jetty, there is an arcade machine called Pelican Panic. It is older than my parents. The paint on the side has faded, the joystick wobbles, and you need an actual coin to play, which my little sister thinks is hilarious. But it works perfectly, and every time I play it, I am five years old again. When I was little, my grandpa used to bring me to the jetty every Friday after school. He would buy us a bucket of chips, lift me onto an upturned milk crate, and let me play Pelican Panic while he read the paper. He always cheered when I beat level three, even though I'm fairly sure he never once looked up. Grandpa moved to Queensland last year, and I miss him a lot. So now, whenever I'm at the jetty, I put one coin in, and for those few minutes I can almost smell his newspaper and feel the milk crate wobbling under my feet. For me, that old arcade machine is a time machine. Some kids say it's a waste of a coin. They're wrong. I still have never beaten level four, but my little sister has, which she mentions often.
encounters.prompt: In his first draft, Zed called the arcade machine 'a photo album'. Why is 'a time machine' the stronger metaphor?
encounters.success: An album only shows old pictures. Zed can almost smell Grandpa's newspaper and feel the milk crate. He's back there.

options.text: An album is quiet. A time machine sounds exciting, like an arcade game.
options.reason: Exciting isn't the point. Zed can almost smell the newspaper. Playing takes him back.

options.text: He doesn't just look at the past. He feels he's back there, aged five.
A time machine goes both ways, so Zed can dream about beating level four one day.
options.reason: Zed only goes back, to Fridays with Grandpa. Nothing in his piece is about the future.

options.text: A time machine sounds old and battered, just like the faded paint and wobbly joystick.
options.reason: The machine's looks aren't the point. Zed says playing it makes him five again.
